tool_priority: get_trace (inspect full slow trace chains and critical path across sampled traces)
query_metrics (compare latency, db_qps, redis and pool metrics trends/windows)
inspect_redis (snapshot keyspace hit/miss, TTLs, and hot keys across repeated samples)
inspect_database (identify top query latency, blocking, plan for product lookup/list queries)

stop_conditions: Confirm or rule out inventory-service/postgres/redis as bottleneck via trace critical path plus latency metrics.
No evidence of active DB blocking, queueing, or Redis miss spike worsening across two consecutive snapshots.
Kafka/Redpanda consumer lag stays at 0 and errors remain 0.
If all HTTP health healthy and no current pool waiting, treat as steady-state unless latency trend increases.
initial_hypotheses: Latency is concentrated in nested gateway->order-service->inventory-service checkout path; inventory-service GET /products span (~33ms) dominates downstream time.

inventory-service shows large cumulative pool errors/queueing/wait (441 errors, 874 queued, 525760ms wait) and Redis keyspace miss-heavy stats (612630 misses vs 121851 hits) suggesting cache coldness or thundering misses.
Database inspection shows repeated product lookups (SELECT ... FROM products WHERE id=$1 calls_delta 322) and a product list/order-by id query, hinting DB/query or cache-driven latency.
Kafka/Redpanda lag is 0 and payment/user/notification services are fast and error-free, so impact appears localized to checkout read path, not event pipeline.
